# Open Conduct

> Open Conduct is the public standard behind the proposed Conduct Quotient. It documents the components, protections, decisions, evidence, open questions, and path to research. Version 0.5 is a developed proposal, not an operating standard or certified system.

## Current standard

- [Conduct Quotient 0.5](https://openconduct.org/standard/0.5/conduct-quotient): How qualifying Net Conduct Score and Verified Conduct Index inputs could produce one private contextual score.
- [Net Conduct Score](https://openconduct.org/netconductscore): The proposed open measure of human experience in an eligible, verified interaction.
- [Verified Conduct Index 0.5](https://openconduct.org/standard/0.5/verified-conduct-index): The approved-record input for eligible responsibilities within a customer's control.
- [The case for a standard](https://openconduct.org/case-for-conduct): Why customer conduct needs a shared standard rather than a private company feature, what a participating business might get, what a reward is allowed to be, and what survives if portability never clears review.
- [Protections and prohibited uses](https://openconduct.org/protections): Required limits, rights, remedies, and uses the proposal rejects.
- [Regulatory posture](https://openconduct.org/regulatory-posture): Which law each design decision is answering, which questions remain unresolved, and the legal work required before any pilot. Issue-spotting, not legal advice.

## Project record

- [Research and decisions](https://openconduct.org/library): The current specification, decision register, open questions, adversarial review, and synthetic research.
- [Download the complete v0.5 public record](https://openconduct.org/downloads/open-conduct-v0.5-public-record.zip): The versioned specification, decisions, open questions, architecture records, adversarial audit, and synthetic research Suites A–L, with checksums.
- [Status and governance](https://openconduct.org/status): What exists, what does not, and who stewards the work today.
- [Contribute](https://openconduct.org/contribute): How to challenge or improve the proposal.
- [Historical Conduct Quotient 0.4](https://openconduct.org/standard/0.4/conduct-quotient): Superseded historical proposal; excluded from search indexing.

## Core model

Net Conduct Score (NCS) records eligible employees' experience of working with a customer. Its bounded question asks whether, based only on how the customer interacted with people, the worker would want to serve that customer again. The draft uses four directional responses with no midpoint and includes a safe abstention path.

Verified Conduct Index (VCI) uses approved records about responsibilities a customer accepted and could control. Records must pass source, identity, responsibility, evidence, duplication, notice, correction, and dispute rules before they can qualify.

Conduct Quotient (CQ) combines independently qualifying NCS and VCI inputs into one private score for one named context. The working display runs from 1.00 to 5.00. Confidence, evidence sufficiency, recency, disputes, patterns, and context affect whether a score can be shown. If the evidence does not qualify, the system shows a status instead of inventing a number.

## Benefit scope

The reward catalog is open-ended and governed reward by reward. A participating business may decide how generously to recognize customers, and each proposed benefit is classified before it is offered. The first benefit in a pilot is deliberately modest because a first pilot tests whether the mechanism is safe, fair, and understandable rather than whether the reward is appealing. That restriction describes the first step rather than a permanent ceiling. One boundary never opens at any tier: complaints, refunds, corrections, disputes, appeals, accommodations, and safety responses are rights rather than rewards, and Conduct cannot change their speed, order, or availability. Baseline service cannot be degraded so that a recognized experience looks better by comparison.

## Benefit-delivery boundary

Conduct governs whether a consumer qualifies for one approved additional benefit and produces the minimum purpose-specific result. Existing loyalty, promotion, commerce, or customer-experience systems may deliver that benefit. They ordinarily receive only eligibility, purpose, policy version, and expiry—not CQ, NCS, VCI, source companies, worker responses, or event history. Talon.One is one example of this replaceable partner category; no partnership or endorsement exists today.

## Non-negotiable direction

- No public profiles or searchable rankings.
- No universal moral score.
- No automatic cross-company portability.
- No negative external result for choosing not to share or not qualifying.
- No high-stakes use involving employment, housing, credit, insurance, healthcare, education, government benefits, policing, immigration, or essential services.
- No central cross-company history warehouse as the operating model.
- People and workers need notice, understandable explanations, correction, challenge, escalation, and exit paths.
- Receiving businesses ordinarily learn only whether a person qualifies for one approved additional benefit; the underlying score and history stay private.

## Legal posture

Section 13 of the working specification carries the legal and ethical design constraints, and the regulatory-posture page summarizes them. Consumer control, a positive-only output, nonprofit governance, selective disclosure, and open publication each reduce specific legal risk. None functions as immunity. Consumer reporting, social scoring, automated decisions, disability and public accommodations, privacy, competition, labor, biometrics, and public-claim treatment all require jurisdiction- and use-specific review by qualified counsel before any real person is affected. No such review has been completed.

## Current status

Brent Turner currently stewards the proposal from Massachusetts. No operating Open Conduct Alliance exists. No one can receive a Conduct Quotient, issue an official Net Conduct Score, join an alliance, buy a network report, or claim certification. Real-world validity, fairness, legal, cultural, labor, accessibility, security, governance, and product research remain ahead.
